title: Clinician Recommendations for Behavioral Interventions in ADHD: A Call to Action for Applied Behavior Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is characterized by persistent pattens of inattention and/or hyperactivity‐impulsivity that interfere with functioning or development. Pediatric guidelines call for the combination of behavioral intervention and stimulant medication to treat ADHD. We conducted a survey among caregivers of children with ADHD to identify interventions recommended to treat ADHD by their diagnostic clinician. Seventy percent of caregivers reported that medication was recommended. Most caregivers reported that some form of behavioral intervention was recommended, but only 14% reported they received a recommendation for applied behavior analysis, specifically. In addition, the number of caregivers reporting a clinician recommendation for applied behavior analysis decreased as children aged. We discuss the potential of applied behavior analysis with this population and suggest some things that behavior analysts can do to increase their work with individuals with ADHD.
